title: Example 1: an invoice exceeds goods received

text: Example 1: an invoice exceeds goods received
Illustrative distributor. All amounts below exclude tax.
KRIYOPAY
₹10,000 under review
Store confirms the shortage. Finance requests a corrected bill or receipt evidence before approval.
The system flags the mismatch. An authorized reviewer decides the documented resolution.

Constructed example. PO 100 units × ₹1,000 = ₹100,000. GRN confirms only 90. Invoice requests 100. Difference 10 × ₹1,000 = ₹10,000. This is a disputed exposure held for resolution, not a proven saving. Tax and TDS treatment require accountant review.

₹18,000 acquisition spend ÷ 3 customers = ₹6,000 CAC
Founder demos and accountant referrals lead with one workflow. Expansion follows measured adoption.
Pilot scope: 20 realistic invoices with known exceptions, or a small reviewed transport settlement cohort.

Assumed funnel: 100 qualified prospects × 20% = 20 demos. 20 × 25% = 5 pilots. 5 × 60% = 3 paid companies. If sales and marketing spend is ₹18,000, CAC is ₹6,000 per paid company. These are targets to validate, not pipeline data. Direct selling can still sell SaaS subscriptions.

title: Why avoid a standard one-time licence?

text: Why avoid a standard one-time licence?
Here, “direct product sale” means an upfront licence. Direct sales can also sell SaaS.
KRIYOPAY
A negotiated enterprise licence can still fit special deployments. SaaS contribution assumes 36 paid months.

Interpretation of user question. Illustrative comparison assumes upfront licence ₹60,000, onboarding ₹3,000, acquisition ₹6,000, annual support cost ₹12,000 for three years. SaaS ₹2,999/month for 36 months, delivery cost ₹600/month, onboarding ₹3,000, acquisition ₹6,000. Both exclude fixed R&D, tax and financing. No churn, bad debt or discounts in this comparison.

title: Customer ROI at the Growth price

text: Customer ROI at the Growth price
Illustrative 400-invoice SME using the review-time assumptions from slide 3
KRIYOPAY
Monthly capacity value
Net value after ₹3,499 subscription
4.57× benefit / subscription
₹5,000 proposed onboarding fee ÷ ₹12,501 = 0.40-month simple payback
Capacity value is not guaranteed cash savings. Excludes adoption time, customer taxes and disputed invoice exposure.

All inputs assumed. 400 × (12 − 4) / 60 = 53.333 hours monthly. × ₹300 = ₹16,000 monthly capacity value. Less ₹3,499 subscription = ₹12,501 net monthly capacity value. Ratio 16,000/3,499 = 4.5727. Net benefit / subscription = 357.27%. At illustrative onboarding fee ₹5,000, simple payback = 5,000 / 12,501 = 0.40 months after steady-state adoption. This onboarding fee is proposed and not the internal onboarding cost used elsewhere.

title: Unit economics per active company

Planning assumptions for monthly subscriptions. No annual discount in this model.
KRIYOPAY
CAC ₹6,000 / ₹2,399 = 2.50 months. Including ₹3,000 internal onboarding cost: 3.75 months.

Revenue mix assumes 50% Starter, 30% Growth, 20% Control. ARPA = 0.5×1499 + 0.3×3499 + 0.2×5999 = ₹2,999. Monthly direct cost assumptions: infrastructure ₹100, AI/storage ₹160, support delivery ₹250, payment cost allowance ₹90, total ₹600. Contribution ₹2,399, margin 79.993%. CAC ₹6,000, simple contribution payback 2.501 months, plus ₹3,000 internal onboarding gives 3.752 months. Fixed payroll excludes support already allocated as direct cost.

title: Commercial recommendation

text: Commercial recommendation
A focused paid pilot provides the evidence for the next investment.
KRIYOPAY
Start with one measurable workflow

Sell a monthly company subscription through founder-led demos.
Configure each customer’s package and usage limits explicitly.
Scale after customers renew and delivery costs support the margin.

Recommendation, not an approved execution plan. First target either invoice exceptions or driver finance with a defined buyer. Validate repeat usage and willingness to pay before scaling. Suggested pilot measures are targets, not results.
